answer.rationale: Write path p99 is 5x target, a release went out 2 hours ago, and settlement traffic is at its daily peak with heavy writes. b1 documents that rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike with the prior build stable and no customer impact. b3 also documents that provisioning headroom absorbed a retail peak with queue depth flat, so capacity headroom may already exist — but the time-to-effect on add_capacity under a latency climb during peak writes is longer than a rollback. A single intervention should be the one with the fastest, most bounded recovery that preserves writes. Verifying b1 confirms the rollback mechanism worked cleanly here before. Rollback is the highest-confidence, fastest mitigation for a release-induced write-path regression while customer writes are at peak.
